Thanks for pulling this together, Marissa. I took a quick pass on the sheet and sketched a priority ladder approach — notes below.

Proposal (short):
- Priority Tiering: Tier 1 = strategic (revenue > $2M ARR OR active PoC + exec sponsorship); Tier 2 = high-fit (>$500k ARR or proof-of-concept stalled); Tier 3 = nurture.
- Routing rule: If AtlasOps is marked "partner_lead" and partner_introduced_pipeline >= 50% => partner-first routing; else Redwood-first with partner notification within 24hrs.
- Conflict resolution column: "tie_breaker_owner" — values: Partner, Redwood, Joint. If Joint, set a 2-week joint outreach cadence.

I've left comments on three accounts where the "source_of_truth" differs. Suggest we lock an authoritative mapping (HubSpot canonical name) to avoid back-and-forth.

Link to my working sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1a2b3cAtlasOpsCrosswalk (drive)

Happy to join the Monday triage.

— Jonas
Director, Alliances | Redwood Inference

All — a couple operational guardrails from my side (sales ops + partner program):

1) Ownership rule (recommended):
   - Partner owns if: partner_introduced_pipeline >= 50% OR partner_paid_PoC = true OR co-signed SOW exists.
   - Redwood owns if none of the above.
2) Exclusive holds: limit exclusivity to 90 days and require a signed MOU. If we see two logos where AtlasOps has already paid for PoCs, we can negotiate exclusivity for the pilot window.
3) Escalation: disputes escalate to Regional VP (cc list) after 7 days of unresolved tie-break.

I suggest we ask Procurement at both parties to pre-clear the MOU template so legal turnaround is <5 business days. I'll open a request with Procurement and loop in Legal.

Karthik
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
